messages.content:
Passages:

[api-limits] Each API key is limited to 60 requests per minute on Starter, 600 on Pro and a negotiated limit on Enterprise. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header; clients should back off exponentially and honour the header. Monthly call quotas are separate from per-minute limits and are shown on the usage page; when a quota is exhausted, requests return 402 until the next cycle or until the plan is upgraded. Webhook deliveries do not count toward the quota.

[plans] Starter includes up to 5 seats, 10,000 API calls per month and community support. Pro includes unlimited seats at a per-seat price, 250,000 API calls per month, SSO, audit logs and email support with a one-business-day response target. Enterprise adds a custom API quota, dedicated support with a four-hour response target, data residency options and a signed DPA. Upgrades apply immediately and are prorated; downgrades apply at the next renewal.

[security-incident] If you believe you have found a vulnerability or that your account has been compromised, email security@ (or use the in-app 'Report a security issue' link) rather than opening a normal ticket. Include what you observed, the time, and any request IDs. We acknowledge reports within 24 hours and do not take action against good-faith researchers. For a suspected account compromise, also rotate your API keys immediately from Settings > API keys and enable SSO enforcement if available.

Answer:
When you go over your API rate limit, you receive an HTTP 429 status code with a Retry-After header. Clients should back off exponentially and honor the header [api-limits].
